frozen_question: Is requirement extraction reproducible across repeated runs on the same frozen job postings under the frozen extraction contract?

metric_definitions.identity_tuple: (name, type, importance, category, years_required, evidence_status, work_condition) as persisted by canonical_requirements[].identity
metric_definitions.identity_set_stability: all three runs' full 7-field identity sets are equal
metric_definitions.name_set_stability: all three runs' field-0 sets are equal (selection unit)
metric_definitions.jaccard: J(A,B)=|A n B|/|A u B|; empty union returns None (undefined)
metric_definitions.selection_denominator: two distinct denominators reported and never mixed: UNIQUE identities per job, and total run-level requirement occurrences (sum of the three counts)
metric_definitions.classification_alignment: exact field-0 name match; a name must appear in >=2 of 3 runs to be classified as aligned
metric_definitions.evidence_audit: mechanical quote-correspondence only: normalised substring check of requirement source_text inside the frozen posting. PRELIMINARY -- does not adjudicate semantic support
metric_definitions.missing_data: runs without persisted raw/coerced extraction or usage are reported as null/absent; never imputed

D_evidence.root_cause_of_missing_evidence: The extraction schema binds source_text to the structured requirement lists (experience/education/location/other) but not to required_skills or preferred_skills, which are list[str]. SKILL-type requirements are therefore unevidenced by construction, not by model omission. Persisted raw extraction confirms the model emitted 580 bare-string skill items and 492 dict items carrying source_text.
D_evidence.semantic_support_adjudication: NOT PERFORMED -- cannot be established mechanically

E_score.causality: correlation between extraction change and score change is reported as co-occurrence only; no causal claim is made

G_execution_anomalies.connection_to_extraction_variability: NOT ESTABLISHED -- no persisted evidence links provider execution anomalies to extraction variability; reported separately
